A1.justification: Both PDFs describe iTool and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original BFCL and API-Bank evaluations, component ablations, training-data scaling experiments, and preference-optimization comparisons.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds dataset-generalization, model-size scaling, computational-cost, and additional ablation results.

M1.justification: The curriculum warm-up, perplexity-based sampling, step-level MCTS preferences, and iterative SimPO procedure remain unchanged. The revised PUCT equation and added explanation clarify the existing method without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds xLAM as a training corpus alongside ToolACE. BFCL-half reuses already covered BFCL-Live data under a new split; the tool-use tasks and BFCL/API-Bank evaluation coverage otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds the base SFT + IRT comparator, enabling comparison with reinforcement learning without curriculum warm-up. Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 and the appendix preference-algorithm comparison remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a 50/50 BFCL-Live training/test split, averaging Live and Multi-turn scores, controlled SFT data-scale sweeps across 3B/8B/32B models, and a runtime comparison. Table 3 also adds a control without curriculum warm-up. The original main training proportions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 substantially expands supplementary analysis through the additional Table 3 ablation, synthetic versus non-synthetic training-data analysis in Section 4.5, cost-benefit analysis in Appendix B.2, and model-size dependence of SFT saturation in Appendix B.3. Existing MCTS, iteration-count, and preference-algorithm analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The reported MCTS seed remains 42, and neither version introduces repeated-evaluation run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 5 averages evaluation metrics, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4 retain their scores. New results include the Table 3 comparator scores 88.86/76.51/20.65, cross-dataset results such as xLAM 8B SFT 42.74 versus iTool 48.47, Figure 9 model-size curves, and the 10-hour SFT baseline cost. Table 3 also changes gain annotations, including 9.6 to 7.8 for Non-live SFT.

T1.justification: Equation 5 changes the PUCT maximization variable from s_t to action a and explicitly defines the successor state n(s_t,a) in the visit-count denominator. This is a limited formal correction; the remaining mathematical definitions and objectives are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central problem, proposed contributions, and headline performance claims. Additional experiments support those claims without redefining their stated scope.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations that benefits extend across training datasets but are larger on synthetic data, SFT saturation persists across model sizes, and the additional runtime offers favorable cost-effectiveness. The original limitations remain unchanged, including the now-unreconciled single-dataset statement.

D1.justification: v5 adds a code-repository link, explicitly describes random selection of the 90% warm-up subset, defines base SFT as using the entire gold-labeled dataset, and reports its 10-hour cost. Existing LoRA/QLoRA settings, MCTS parameters, hardware, and 28-hour iTool training disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion retain the same works and research positioning. Using the already cited xLAM dataset in a new experiment does not introduce a new related-work contribution.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized wording and terminology corrections, updates affiliations, adds acknowledgements and experimental subsections, and moves the former Appendix B.2 preference analysis to B.4. The main narrative and section sequence are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v5 expands Table 3, adds Tables 5 and 8 and Figure 9, and reformats several retained plots. Figure 8 gains separate legends for both panels. The overall two-column design and most existing displays remain intact, with appendix items renumbered or relocated.

improvement.justification: v5 improves component attribution through the added SFT + IRT control and broadens evidence about data dependence, SFT saturation, and computational cost. It also adds a code link. The gain is limited by sparse details for new experiments, unreconciled 3B ToolACE averages between Tables 4 and 5, and the unchanged single-dataset limitation.
